topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: Introduces the lecture and outlines its learning objectives regarding the modes of action and approaches in cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: Examines standard modalities of cancer treatment, covering their therapeutic mechanisms, clinical successes, and limitations due to systemic toxicity and drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting tumor-specific vulnerabilities and defects
topics.groupedBecause: Details therapeutic strategies designed to exploit cancer-specific biological vulnerabilities, including hormone receptor dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: Focuses on therapies targeting hyperactivated oncogenic kinases, exploring oncogene addiction, structural drug design, and mechanisms of acquired resistance and drug dependency.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: Discusses antibody-based therapies designed to bind cell-surface targets and either recruit immune effector mechanisms or deliver cytotoxic payloads directly to tumor cells.

topics.label: Harnessing the immune system: checkpoint inhibition and cellular immunotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: Explores cancer immunotherapies that engage or engineer the host immune system, encompassing immune checkpoint blockade, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, historical progress, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: Synthesizes the overarching challenges in treating heterogeneous tumors, historical improvements in patient survival, and emerging ethical and therapeutic considerations.
